author: Erica Kollmann
title: Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia With 3 House Committees Waiting: ‘How Could He Possibly Do the Job?’
teaser: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO but faces congressional testimony and multiple probes as the company heads into GTC DC.
body:
Jensen Huang is back running Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), though a good part of his calendar now belongs to Washington. 

On Dec. 1, the day he was originally slated to deliver the GTC DC keynote, Huang will sit for a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the CCP and the Select Committee on Intelligence.

  • NVDA stock is moving. Get all the details you need to trade it. 

Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned on Nov. 12 amid affair allegations tied to Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

Nvidia stock closed 31.48% higher at $165.05 on Monday after the announcement. Addressing cheering employees at headquarters, Huang said he would be “a better CEO the second time around.”

A Docket Full of Probes

The House interviews open a crowded stretch of oversight that runs straight through Nvidia’s conference week. 

Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott (R-S.C.) said Huang will also testify publicly as the sole witness at a Dec. 3 hearing on U.S. export controls.

California’s attorney general is investigating Huang’s remarks, and there is a Department of Justice investigation along with a reported SEC probe. Huang still has to cooperate with the board’s own review, led by law firm Wachtell Lipton.

Yale School of Management senior associate dean Jeff Sonnenfeld questioned whether any executive could run a company under so much scrutiny. “How could he possibly do the job?” he told CNBC.

Katten Chair Gil Soffer, a former federal prosecutor, said nothing prevents Huang from doing his day job but warned the investigations require serious preparation. “You don’t just walk in cold,” Soffer said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC he was central to convincing the board to bring Huang back, a role likely to draw more fire from Democrats already probing Nvidia’s chip sales.

Read Also: Tesla Vs. SpaceX: Which Elon Musk Stock Has the Stronger Setup?

Off-Key Note

Nvidia still needs to sell customers, partners and suppliers on its AI roadmap at GTC DC, where Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, currently holds Huang’s old keynote slot.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Chipping Away at the Crown

Investors have worried Nvidia’s pace of innovation could slow without its founder, even with products for the next two years fully designed. 

Major customers, including Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), are building their own chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia and rein in AI costs.

The political fallout could start to touch Nvidia’s sales as well, with the Commerce Department moving last week to stop Chinese firms from renting Nvidia chips across borders to sidestep export controls. 

NVDA Stock Price Activity: Nvidia stock was down 8.60% at $150.86 on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro market data.

author: Piero Cingari
title: Anthropic Drops Below IPO Prices, Nvidia Sinks 7% After Record Rally: Stock Market Today
teaser: Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price and Nvidia gave back 30% of its record gain, while health care, retailers and the Dow rallied.
body:
The artificial-intelligence trade cracked on two fronts Tuesday. Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) slipped below its $83 IPO price less than a week after its record debut, while Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) handed back nearly a third of Monday’s record gain. Investors rotated into health care, retailers and the blue-chip Dow.

The chip reversal came a day after the comeback. Nvidia soared 31.5% on Monday, but Chinese state media said Jensen Huang‘s return as Nvidia CEO was unlikely to ease U.S. export curbs. The Commerce Department blacklisted seven companies, including an Alibaba unit, in a probe into alleged transfers of Nvidia chips to China.

Nvidia fell 7.2% to $153.19, erasing about $267 billion in market value, or 30% of Monday’s gain. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) dropped 7.1%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) lost 8%.

  • The S&P 500 fell 1% to 7,167, down 71 points.
  • The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 188 points, or 0.4%, to 49,783.
  • The Nasdaq 100 slid 2.7% to 26,034, down 713 points.
  • Within the Magnificent Seven, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) bucked the selloff with a 1.5% gain, even after a 24-hour service outage.
  • The Russell 2000 rose 0.6% to 2,685, and the CBOE Volatility Index climbed 5.7% to 28.13.

Read Also: All Is Right Again? Wall Street Splits on What Jensen Huang's Return Really Fixes

Bonds Rally As Chipmakers Sank

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5 basis points to 4.89%. The 2-year yield slipped 3 basis points to 4.66%, and the 30-year yield eased 3 basis points to 5.28%.

Gold dropped 2.4% to $3,564 an ounce, and silver tumbled 5.8% to $40.68. Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell 1.9% to $60,007. West Texas Intermediate crude edged up 0.4% to $80.52 a barrel, while Brent slid 2.3% to $87.29.

On the data front, the Conference Board’s consumer confidence index jumped to 103.3 in November from 91.9, far above the 92.5 forecast and its highest level since January 2025.

Tuesday’s Performance In Major US Indices

According to the Benzinga Pro platform:

  • The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:VOO) fell 0.6%.
  • The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA) rose 0.6%.
  • The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) dropped 2%.
  • The iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSE:IWM) added 0.5%.

Health Care Leads

  • State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSE:XLV) rose 2.8%, the top sector, as a $41 billion takeover lifted drugmakers and investors rotated out of chips.
  • State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (NYSE:XBI) jumped 5.1%.
  • State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSE:XLK) lost 3.4%, the worst sector, as chipmakers gave back Monday’s rally.
  • State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSE:XLP) gained 2.1% and industrials were the only other sector in the red.
  • State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF (NYSE:XRT) advanced 3% on upbeat retail earnings.

Among the Gainers

Nike Inc. (NYSE:NKE) led the blue-chip index with a 5.8% gain.

Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc. (NYSE:DKS) rallied 16.5%. Third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.94 per share beat the $1.38 consensus and the retailer raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook to $11.45-$12.30 per share. The company reported a rebound in sales at Foot Locker, one of the country’s biggest sneaker sellers.

Amentum Holdings Inc. (NYSE:AMTM) surged 19.8% after fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 71 cents per share topped the 66-cent estimate and it authorized its first-ever buyback, of up to $500 million.

Insmed Inc. (NASDAQ:INSM) climbed 14.2% after Sanofi (NASDAQ:SNY) agreed to buy the respiratory drugmaker for $175 per share in cash.

Pinterest Inc. (NYSE:PINS) rose 12.2% after a filing showed it amended change-in-control severance terms for Chief Executive William Ready. Dollar Tree Inc. (NASDAQ:DLTR) gained 12.1% after third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share beat the 91-cent estimate and it raised its full-year outlook.

Read Also: Big Tech Just Became a Value Trade — Something Wall Street Hasn't Seen in 20 Years

On the Downside

Anthropic fell 9.8% to $79.06, 29% below the $111.50 open on Nov. 19. A regulatory filing on Monday showed Chief Executive Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares, worth over $280 million, the day after the listing. Wedbush Securities started coverage Tuesday with an Outperform rating and a $120 price target.

In Elon Musk‘s orbit, Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) fell 5.4% to $126.21 and Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) slipped 0.6% to $383.08 after the Financial Times reported that the two companies named five directors to special committees negotiating a merger, with the aim of reaching a deal before year-end. SpaceX is valued at more than $1.8 trillion and Tesla at about $1.5 trillion, which would make it the largest corporate merger on record.

Analog Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:ADI) sank 17.5%. Fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $4.06 per share beat estimates by 18 cents, but its first-quarter guidance of $3.82 per share was only in line.

Semtech Corp. (NASDAQ:SMTC) fell 16.7% despite record quarterly sales of $423 million, up 58%. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (NYSE:HPE) dropped 16.4% after Chief Financial Officer Marie Myers said gross margin may soften through fiscal 2027 as AI systems take a larger share of sales, overshadowing a beat.

Dycom Industries Inc. (NYSE:DY) slid 14.8% on its fourth-quarter outlook, despite record revenue of $2.06 billion. Astera Labs Inc. (NASDAQ:ALAB) lost 13.1% as AI connectivity stocks unwound Monday’s rally.

author: Chris Katje
title: Dow Outperforms Nike Stock 100x Since Inclusion: Jay Woods Expects 'Underperformer' to Get the Boot
teaser: Changes to the Dow Jones Industrial Average coming in 2027? Market expert Jay Woods says it has a history of "kicking out underperformers."
body:
Freedom Capital Markets Chief Market Strategist Jay Woods has an impressive history of picking stocks that will be replaced in the the Dow Jones Industrial Average , previously calling for Walgreens Boots Alliance and Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC) to be replaced.

Nike Inc (NYSE:NKE) could get the boot next in 2027, Woods told Benzinga.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average added the sneaker company on Sept. 23, 2013. It replaced Alcoa (NYSE:AA) at the time. Since that date, Nike stock has posted a 2.2% gain. Compare that to the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average (NYSE:DIA), which tracks the index. The ETF is up 221.1% over the same time period, outperforming by 100x.

"The Dow has had a history of kicking out underperformers and then when it gets kicked out, there’s your time to buy," Woods added. Over the last two years, the Dow replaced four of the 30 components in the index.

Which Company Replaces Nike?

Nike shares are at 12-year lows. If the index replaces it, Woods expects it will be with a stock from the same sector — apparel and footwear.

"They’ll probably go with a high-end retailer,” he said. “TJ Maxx has had a great run over time. Maybe they go that route. If they want to go shoes, Crocs, that’s a nice uptrend still over years."

TJX Companies (NYSE:TJX) stock is up 107% over the last five years. Crocs (NASDAQ:CROX) shares are down over the last five years but have posted a 97% gain over the last year.

Compare that to Nike shares, which are down 42.7% over the last year and down 78.9% over the last five years.  

As for a buying opportunity, Woods highlights Intel and ExxonMobil (NYSE:XOM). The Dow dropped ExxonMobil in favor of Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) in August 2020. It then swapped Intel for Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) in November 2024.

Read Also: SpaceX, Tesla Merger Could Hit Democratic Roadblock: Jay Woods Unsure if Elon Musk Can 'Work His Magic'

Recent Dow Changes

Founded in 1896, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has gone through many changes.

In 2013, Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) and Visa Inc (NYSE:V) replaced Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and Hewlett Packard (NYSE:HPE) in the index.

Changes also took place in 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 (x2), 2024 (x2) and 2026. Recent changes involved some of the world’s biggest companies, weighting the Dow Jones Industrial Average toward Big Tech.

In 2024, Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) replaced Walgreens Boots. That same year, Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) replaced Intel and Sherwin-Williams (NYSE:SHW) also replaced Dow Inc (NYSE:DOW).

The last change to the index came earlier this year in June with Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) replacing Verizon Inc (NYSE:VZ). A move to replace Nike in 2027 would mark the first back-to-back changes to the index since 2019 and 2020, part of a four-year stretch with changes every year.

title: Why Is Salesforce Stock Surging on Tuesday?
teaser: Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE: CRM) stock rises Tuesday during a broader technology sell-off as traders move capital from AI names like Nvidia into established software stocks.
body:
Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) stock is trading higher on Tuesday as market participants shift funds out of artificial intelligence stocks and into traditional enterprise software.

• What is CRM trading at now?

The decline comes amid broader weakness across the technology sector, with artificial intelligence chipmaker NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) falling approximately 7.54% on Tuesday as investors booked profits following Monday’s rally.

On Tuesday, the Nasdaq fell 2.50%, while the S&P 500 declined 1.02%, with technology emerging as the weakest-performing sector, posting a 3.9% loss.

Sector Trends

Despite the technology downturn, overall market breadth remains positive, showing seven advancing sectors against four declining sectors.

Defensive sectors lead Tuesday’s gains, with Health Care rising 2.37% and Consumer Staples adding 1.75%, keeping the Dow Jones Industrial Average nearly flat with a 0.02% dip.

Salesforce’s Tuesday advance occurs after an extended period of sector weakness. Over the past 30 days, the Technology sector declined 16.27% and it dropped 14.67% over the past 90 days.

Read Also: Big Tech Just Became a Value Trade — Something Wall Street Hasn't Seen in 20 Years

Wall Street Analyst Ratings

Across 31 covering analysts, 23 rate Salesforce stock a Buy, seven rate it a Hold, and one rates it a Sell. The average analyst price forecast stands at $272.77, representing a 41.5% upside from current trading levels, with individual forecasts ranging from $165 to $400.

Recent analyst updates include Citigroup maintaining a Neutral rating while lowering its price target to $198 on Monday, TD Cowen retaining its Buy rating while reducing its price target to $275 on Monday and BTIG maintaining a Buy rating while cutting its price target to $250 on Nov. 18.

Technical Analysis

From a trend perspective, CRM is still working uphill: it’s trading 8.6% below its 20-day SMA ($211.92) and 14.7% below its 50-day SMA ($226.97), keeping the intermediate trend bearish until those levels are reclaimed.

At the same time, price is only 2.1% below the 200-day SMA ($197.73), so this zone is acting like a "line in the sand" where dip-buyers may try to defend the longer-term trend.

The longer-term backdrop is mixed: the 50-day SMA remains above the 200-day SMA (a Golden Cross that occurred in September), but the 20-day SMA is below the 50-day SMA, which reflects the more recent downshift in trend.

Key turning points also frame the range — there was a recent swing high in September and a swing low in November, and the stock is still down 14.65% over the past 12 months.

  • Key Resistance: $220 — Round-number ceiling that also sits near the stock’s 20-day/100-day moving-average area where rebounds can stall
  • Key Support: $171 — Nearby floor tied to a prior pivot zone where buyers previously stepped in

author: Evette Mitkov
title: Nike Stock Jumps Amid Foot Locker's Positive Q3 Insights
teaser: Nike Inc. (NYSE: NKE) shares are moving higher Tuesday after Dick's Sporting Goods pointed to progress in its Foot Locker turnaround.
body:
Nike Inc. (NYSE:NKE) shares are moving higher Tuesday after Dick’s Sporting Goods pointed to progress in its Foot Locker turnaround. Here’s what you should know.

  • Nike stock is charging ahead with explosive momentum. What’s behind NKE gains?

Nike Stock Rises On Dick’s Foot Locker Comments

Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc. (NYSE:DKS) Executive Chairman Ed Stack endorsed Nike’s decision to release products less often, calling it the right move for the Jordan brand. Stack described Jordan as weak and said it has been one reason the Foot Locker recovery is running behind Dick’s timeline.

Stack credited Nike for making a long-term decision instead of chasing short-term quarterly results. Stack also said the Nike brand is performing well at Foot Locker, Bloomberg reported.

Two possible benefits stand out for Nike. Core Nike products are selling at a retailer still in the middle of a turnaround, which could point to healthy demand for the brand.

Jordan’s reset has weighed on Foot Locker for now, but Nike could gain over the long run if releasing fewer products restores the brand’s appeal.

Foot Locker’s own results show some progress. Its business grew comparable sales 0.5% in the third quarter, and the U.S. Foot Locker banner rose more than 4%, which Stack called “a particular bright spot.” Dick’s kept its Foot Locker outlook for 2026 unchanged.

NKE Shares Are Popping

NKE Price Action: Nike shares were up 5.86% at $35.74 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro.

author: Surbhi Jain
title: Nvidia Is Helping Finance the AI Boom. Oracle Says It’s Not Betting on Just One Supplier
teaser: Oracle is spreading AI infrastructure financing across suppliers, including Nvidia, as it expands its multibillion-dollar OpenAI buildout.
body:
Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) role in the AI boom may extend beyond supplying the chips that fill data centers. Oracle Corp‘s (NASDAQ:ORCL) latest funding update has put vendor financing back in focus. JPMorgan says Nvidia is part of a broader supplier base helping support the cloud giant’s infrastructure expansion.

But the arrangement is not a one-company bet. Oracle is building its computing stack around far more than Nvidia hardware.

A Wider Financing Network

Oracle said Nov. 20 it had secured all the funding needed to fulfill its infrastructure contract with OpenAI, following a final capital raise earlier this month. The company said the vendor financing outlined at its October Investor Day was already in place, while further private discussions with suppliers were merely additional options. Oracle also said its ability to deliver on the OpenAI contract did not depend on those talks.

JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee said Oracle described its $20 billion raise as “one and done,” with most vendor financing locked in before Investor Day. The financing is spread across many suppliers, with “no over-indexation to any one company,” including Nvidia, says Chatterjee. They said the vendor financing would take the form of receivables. The note does not disclose Nvidia’s individual contribution or identify every participating supplier.

Read Also: Nvidia’s $105 Billion OpenAI Bet Has a 20-Year Catch

Beyond Nvidia’s Chips

The financing picture comes as Oracle widens the range of hardware available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The company has announced plans to offer Alphabet Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) Google TPUs from 2027, alongside Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:AMD) EPYC processors, Cerebras Systems Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:CBRS) inference technology and SambaNova SN50 systems.

It has also made Nvidia’s Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs generally available, with plans to expand Rubin deployments to multi-gigawatt scale. Oracle’s broader roadmap includes Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC)-powered instances and Positron‘s Atlas inference platform.

That mix matters because AI infrastructure is not a single-chip market. Training, inference and agentic workloads place different demands on processors, accelerators, memory and networking. Oracle has said it wants customers to choose among architectures based on performance, power and cost, rather than depend on one configuration. The supplier diversification in its financing arrangements mirrors that broader effort, although Oracle has not said that every technology partner is also a financing provider.

Investment Takeaway

For Nvidia investors, the signal is two-sided. Oracle’s commitment to multi-gigawatt Vera Rubin deployments underscores the scale of its continuing relationship with Nvidia. The vendor-financing structure suggests the capital burden is distributed across a wider ecosystem.

Investors should watch whether Oracle’s infrastructure expansion converts into sustained demand for Nvidia systems—and whether the company can deliver the positive free cash flow it expects in the second half of FY28 and more than $30 billion in FY29. Oracle says it expects to begin self-funding growth in FY29.

title: Bank of America Short Interest Falls From October Peak
teaser: Bank of America Corp. (NYSE:BAC) short sellers pulled back from their positions as the latest report showed a decline from the prior period.Short interest fell 6.43% to 83.05 million shares as of the Oct. 30 settlement
body:
Bank of America Corp. (NYSE:BAC) short sellers pulled back from their positions as the latest report showed a decline from the prior period.

Short interest fell 6.43% to 83.05 million shares as of the Oct. 30 settlement date, from 88.76 million at the Oct. 15 report. That is 1.21% of the float, a 5.47% fall in short interest as a percent of float.

Shorts Retreat From October High

Short interest peaked at 88.76 million shares (1.28% of float) on Oct. 15, and the latest level is 6.43% below that peak. The company reported Q3 2026 results on Oct. 14; EPS came in at $1.08 against a $1.11 estimate. Short interest fell in 1 of the 2 settlement periods that followed.

Days To Cover

Days to cover is 2.23: based on average daily volume, that is how many days it would take short sellers to buy back their shares. Implied average daily volume is about 37.24 million shares, from 46.23 million at the prior report; the rise reflects lighter trading rather than more shorting.

How Bank of America Compares With Peers

According to Benzinga Pro, the average short interest as a percent of float across the 18 peers that reported on the same settlement date is 1.10%, which means Bank of America has higher short interest than its peers on average.

Why Short Interest Matters

Short interest counts shares sold short but not yet covered, and short selling is a bet that the price will fall; rising short interest can signal more bearish sentiment and falling short interest less, but it is not a forecast of the stock’s direction.

BAC Price Action: Bank of America shares were up 0.51% at $48.38 on Tuesday. This is 25.82% below the 52-week high. The stock is down 3.25% since the Oct. 30 settlement date.

title: Symbotic CEO Sees ‘Path To Unlocking’ $5 Billion-Plus Order Beyond $7 Billion Walmart Expansion
teaser: The Symbotic Walmart expansion includes $7 billion in additional work, with a potential 400-store order worth another $5 billion-plus.
body:
Symbotic Inc. (NASDAQ:SYM) said Monday that its expanded agreement with Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) includes about $7 billion in additional work, with a potential 400-store automation deal representing another $5 billion-plus in backlog opportunities.

The Massachusetts-based warehouse automation company outlined the expansion during its fourth-quarter earnings call, following better-than-expected results.

$7 Billion Walmart Expansion And Potential $5 Billion-Plus Order

CEO Rick Cohen said the expanded agreement covers additional automation across the 44 or 45 regional distribution centers included in the original rollout. Symbotic’s next-generation technology will allow Walmart to increase storage capacity at existing facilities.

"We are now installing our SymMicro system for e-commerce fulfillment in two Walmart stores, which moves us closer on the path to unlocking a 400-store order worth another $5 billion-plus to our backlog," Cohen said.

Symbotic has also run software for its two initial prototypes in simulations ahead of a potential wider rollout.

The expanded agreement introduces Symbotic to several new international markets. Cohen highlighted automation opportunities across North and South America but declined to disclose specific project locations.

Read Also: Symbotic Likely To Report Lower Q4 Earnings; These Most Accurate Analysts Revise Forecasts Ahead Of Earnings Call

Earnings Beat And First Profitable Fiscal Year

Symbotic reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 17 cents per share, beating the analyst estimate of 15 cents. Revenue increased 26% year over year to $777.6 million, exceeding the $774.3 million estimate.

GAAP diluted earnings reached 9 cents per share, compared with a 2-cent loss a year earlier.

Adjusted EBITDA increased to $113.9 million from $49.4 million, while adjusted gross margin expanded to 24.8% from 22.1%.

Symbotic achieved its first full year of GAAP profitability, reporting net income of $132.8 million, compared with a $56.9 million loss a year earlier.

Annual revenue increased 25% to $2.8 billion.

Capital Allocation, Backlog And Outlook

Symbotic ended fiscal 2026 with $2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Quarterly operating cash flow declined to $374.6 million from $530.7 million a year earlier, while free cash flow decreased to $353.1 million from $494.4 million.

Cohen said the company sees acquisitions as an opportunity to attract new customers and increase sales, rather than pursuing share repurchases. Management also emphasized expanding recurring revenue.

Despite the expanded partnership, Symbotic identified its dependence on Walmart as a potential business risk.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Symbotic expects revenue of $805 million to $825 million, compared with the $822 million analyst estimate, and adjusted EBITDA of $110 million to $120 million.

The outlook follows a quarter in which the company exceeded earnings and revenue expectations but recorded year-over-year declines in operating and free cash flow.

title: Why Is AMD Stock Plunging Today Despite Strong Wall Street Buy Ratings?
teaser: AMD stock fell over 5% in Tuesday premarket trading as renewed congressional scrutiny of NVIDIA weighed on chipmakers. See how AMD’s 200-day moving average and $642 analyst forecast shape its outlook.
body:
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) stock fell more than 8% in Tuesday trading as renewed congressional scrutiny of NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) pressured semiconductor stocks, while S&P 500 futures declined 0.40%.

Nvidia’s Leadership Crisis Weighs On AMD And Chip Stocks

NVIDIA dropped on Tuesday, reversing part of Monday’s rally following CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.

President Donald Trump intervened to support Huang’s return, and NVIDIA’s board unanimously restored him as president, CEO and director.

However, Republican committee chairmen John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast said the reinstatement failed to resolve outstanding national security concerns.

Lawmakers scheduled interviews with Huang and NVIDIA General Counsel Tim Teter for Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.

Semiconductor ETFs And Rivals Retreat

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) and iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (NASDAQ:SOXX) declined on Tuesday after posting double-digit gains Monday.

SOXX fell approximately 4% after advancing nearly 14% in the previous session.

Other chipmakers, including Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC), also traded lower on Tuesday.

AMD and NVIDIA compete in AI processors but depend on shared manufacturing and packaging capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. (NYSE:TSM). Data centers also combine AMD’s EPYC processors with NVIDIA’s GPUs.

Both companies rely on AI infrastructure spending and face similar supply-chain constraints and U.S. semiconductor export restrictions.

Technical Analysis

AMD has gained 110.86% over the past 12 months but trades below several key moving averages following its recent pullback.

At $429.50, the stock sits 15% below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of $505.19, 22.2% below its 50-day SMA of $552.30 and 18.1% below its 100-day SMA of $524.18.

AMD also trades 0.4% below its 200-day SMA of $431.01, placing the stock near a key long-term technical level.

The 20-day SMA remains below the 50-day SMA, signaling near-term bearish momentum. However, the 50-day SMA continues to hold above the 200-day SMA, indicating that the longer-term bullish structure remains intact.

Analyst Ratings And Price Forecasts

AMD carries a Buy consensus rating with an average analyst price forecast of $642.71 across 50 analysts. Price forecasts range from $540 to $800.

BofA Securities maintained its Buy rating and raised its price forecast to $700 on Nov. 12.

RBC Capital reiterated Sector Perform with a $540 forecast the same day, while William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform.

AMD is still up over 95% on Tuesday, driven by its AI data center business and hyperscaler partnerships.

Nvidia’s Leadership Developments Weigh On Semiconductor Stocks

NVIDIA dropped more than 5% in Tuesday’s premarket session, reversing part of Monday’s rally after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director.

The iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (NASDAQ:SOXX) declined approximately 4% Tuesday after gaining nearly 14% Monday.

Other chipmakers, including Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC), also traded lower. Semiconductor stocks fell roughly 3%–7% after gaining 3%–16% in the previous session.

S&P 500 futures declined 1.1%, adding to broader selling pressure across technology and semiconductor stocks.

Broadcom’s AI Infrastructure Ties To Nvidia

Broadcom and NVIDIA compete in AI processors but also support each other’s data center businesses through complementary computing, networking and enterprise software technologies.

NVIDIA supplies GPUs for AI workloads, while Broadcom develops high-speed networking components that connect processors across large data centers.

Broadcom also integrates NVIDIA’s AI hardware and software into its VMware cloud platform, supporting enterprise AI deployments.

body:
Chevron Corp. (NYSE:CVX) short sellers added to their positions following the company’s Q3 2026 report.

Short interest rose 2.07% to 26.19 million shares as of the Oct. 30 settlement date, from 25.66 million at the Oct. 15 report. That is 1.35% of the float, a 3.85% rise in short interest as a percent of float.

Short Interest Continues To Climb

The company reported Q3 2026 results on Oct. 30; EPS came in at $5.28 against a $4.82 estimate.

Days To Cover

Days to cover is 3.37: based on average daily volume, that is how many days it would take short sellers to buy back their shares. Implied average daily volume is about 7.77 million shares, from 6.97 million at the prior report.

How Chevron Compares With Peers

According to Benzinga Pro, the average short interest as a percent of float across the 10 peers that reported on the same settlement date is 3.10%, which means Chevron has lower short interest than its peers on average.

Why Short Interest Matters

Short interest counts shares sold short but not yet covered, and short selling is a bet that the price will fall. Rising short interest can signal more bearish sentiment and falling short interest less, but it is not a forecast of the stock’s direction.

CVX Price Action: Chevron shares were up 2.10% at $210.49 on Tuesday. This is 10.99% below the 52-week high. The stock is down 10.63% since the Oct. 30 settlement date.
